key_insight: Read-only SQL access to structured perovskite device data raises quantitative question-answering accuracy to about 51%, versus 16–23% for standard passage retrieval.
engineering_relevance: Literature assistants for solar-cell engineering need structured measurement tables to reliably answer questions about performance extrema, distributions, and filtered device counts.
method: Compute 755 ground-truth answers directly from 45,441 measured device records.
Benchmark six retrieval architectures across 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers.
Equip an open 14B language model with read-only SQL access on a single 24 GB GPU.
evidence_signal: SQL-enabled accuracy reached 51.5% on historical literature and 50.8% on prospective literature, compared with 1.6–6.5% zero-shot accuracy.
watch_item: Accuracy remains near 51%, so quantitative outputs still require verification; structured-table completeness and extraction quality are implementation concerns.
paper_title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics
